acceptance_results.evidence: The Windows evidence records a real Electron 44.9.1 window titled RAVEL (isVisible true), a rejected wrong password with no session file written, a real Gateway login as desktop-owner with the real PostgreSQL-backed project 'Catalyst screen', a DPAPI session envelope whose keys are exactly ciphertext/format/version with no plaintext token, a restart restore without a password with a changed SHA-256 refresh-token fingerprint (rotation), and logout deleting the session file followed by a login form after restart. I inspected result.json and the screenshots, re-verified all screenshot hashes, and independently reran the full driver against a database I seeded (ravel_t14_review_test) and a Gateway I started on port 18081: PASS with the same checks and 10 screenshots. The Linux integration cases exercise the same GatewayService/SessionStore classes against a real uvicorn Gateway and real PostgreSQL, including login, owned-project listing, offline restore, reconnect, refresh rotation and logout revoking the refresh token (401). Both the implementer's run-20261020-140104 and my independent run-20261020-141155 pass 8 pytest and 49 Node tests.

As coded and as observed: contextIsolation=true, nodeIntegration=false, sandbox=true, webSecurity=true, webviewTag=false, allowRunningInsecureContent=false, navigateOnDragDrop=false, safeDialogs=true, nodeIntegrationInWorker=false and nodeIntegrationInSubFrames=false; the preload exposes exactly 8 names (connection, listProjects, login, logout, onConnectionStatus, reconnect, session, version) and only ipcRenderer.invoke/on; main-process handlers validate the sender and a hostile same-document renderer using the same preload received 'IPC sender refused'; setWindowOpenHandler denies and will-navigate/will-redirect/will-frame-navigate deny; there is no shell, child_process, @electron/remote, filesystem or environment bridge in apps/desktop/src; the CSP forbids connections, objects, frames, forms and base changes. In both the implementer's and my independent Windows run: window.open returned null, external navigation was blocked, a file:// fetch of .env was blocked, a fetch to a non-configured origin was blocked with attacker request count 0, localStorage/sessionStorage were empty, the DOM contained no JWT-shaped value, and the packaged renderer had the same bridge and no Node globals. The 49 Node tests include the security/contract/session-store suites, and the 5 pytest security cases re-audit both the source and the built bundles.

In my independent Windows run, cutting the loopback proxy produced status Offline and the visible banner 'The Gateway is offline. The Gateway could not be reached.'; Reconnect while down stayed Offline; after restoring transport Reconnect returned Connected and the real project list. After the desktop exited, a direct HTTP login to the same Gateway returned 200 with a session, showing the desktop does not own or stop the server. The Linux integration case stops and restarts the real uvicorn Gateway on a new port and verifies restore, reconnect and logout revocation. LIMIT: this proves Gateway/Supervisor availability after desktop exit, not a full research-agent session; the desktop is a thin client with no Supervisor lifecycle control.

I independently launched the real portable artifact (100,251,514 bytes, SHA256 1878aae1777ccd9eecd1795a791cfd38163f21f525a14afe185c9cf563ea3fa1, PE security directory size 0 so unsigned), observed a real top-level Windows window titled RAVEL belonging to process 'RAVEL Desktop', drove the packaged renderer through the app's own DevTools endpoint, and confirmed its URL is ...\Temp\...\resources\app.asar\dist\renderer\index.html (not a browser page or the development directory). The packaged app rejected a wrong password, logged in to the real Gateway, listed the real project and wrote the DPAPI envelope; renderer screenshots 08/09 and the PrintWindow desktop screenshot 10 show the packaged app. The executable is the reviewed portable x64 build, and the driver recorded the same SHA256/size that certutil reports.

findings.trigger: Run make premium-task TASK=T14 on the Linux gate, then ask what protects the Windows-only Electron window, DPAPI and packaged-launch behavior from regression.
findings.impact: The authoritative Windows GUI and packaged-portable checks are a manually run host driver, not part of the reproducible gate; there is no Windows CI runner. The Linux gate covers the built main-process service, static bundle audits and Node tests only. No acceptance criterion is unmet because the evidence exists and I independently reproduced the whole flow, but a future change could regress a Windows-only surface without failing make premium-task.
findings.required_fix: Add a Windows runner or a mandatory Supervisor integration-checklist step that runs run-electron.cjs with a fresh seed and records result.json for each release candidate.

findings.trigger: Clone the repository and attempt to verify the packaged artifact without rebuilding on Windows.
findings.impact: The 100,251,514-byte portable executable is ignored by apps/desktop/.gitignore:2 and is not retrievable from git, so package acceptance depends on an out-of-band artifact. The recorded SHA256/size and my independent hash verification bind the evidence to this host, but there is no repository-hosted copy.
findings.required_fix: Publish the portable artifact as a retention-controlled release artifact, or record the exact builder image, commit and command used; not required for the internal V0 build.

findings.impact: make lint covers Python only (ruff, pyright). Desktop TypeScript is type-checked by tsc --noEmit inside the Node gate command but has no ESLint/JS lint, so style and some non-type defects are not statically checked.
findings.required_fix: Add an ESLint configuration and lint script to the desktop gate, or record the tsc-only policy as an accepted V0 decision.

findings.trigger: Seed a database for the Windows launch test.
findings.impact: A fixed test password is compiled into the fixture. The script refuses any database not ending in _test and truncates it before seeding, so it cannot touch production state; it is not a product credential.
findings.required_fix: Optional: read the password from an operator-provided environment variable in CI while keeping the _test guard and TRUNCATE.

findings.trigger: Inspect how the packaged renderer is automated.
findings.impact: The portable app is launched with --remote-debugging-port on loopback and driven over CDP; this is a test switch, not a production configuration. Real process/window introspection and a PrintWindow desktop screenshot cross-check the result, but native mouse/keyboard injection is not used.
findings.required_fix: Optional: add a smoke check without the debugging switch (for example process/window plus a UI Automation probe) or document the CDP switch as the accepted harness.

findings.trigger: A renderer attempts to open an external URL, or an operator expects a validated external link to open in the system browser.
findings.impact: V0 denies window.open and all foreign navigation and does not register shell.openExternal, so there is no external-link surface on which to apply the task card's validated external-browser-open step. This is deny-by-default and more restrictive, not a security hole, but the step has no implemented entry point.
findings.required_fix: If an external link is added, validate it against an explicit allowlist in the main process and open it with shell.openExternal; otherwise record the no-external-surface decision in the task record.

findings.trigger: Reproduce the Windows run from the evidence directory alone, after the later pytest gate has reset the shared _test database.
findings.impact: The result records the account username and Gateway loopback origin but not the seed command, database name or Gateway command. My first rerun against the implementer's post-gate database failed authentication because the later pytest fixtures had replaced the seeded account (the stored hash matched the integration fixture password, not the seed default). Re-running seed_account.py with its documented defaults and starting a Gateway against a fresh review database reproduced the entire flow. This is an evidence-completeness/reproducibility gap, not a product defect.
findings.required_fix: Record the exact seed and Gateway commands and the database name in the Windows evidence directory (never the password).

residual_risks: The Windows-only GUI, DPAPI and packaged-launch surface is not regression-gated by make premium-task; it remains a manually run host driver (P2 finding). I reproduced it once, but future candidates need the same run.
The portable executable is ignored by git and cannot be retrieved from the repository; only its SHA256 and size are recorded (P2 finding). Rebuild requires a Windows host and the pinned toolchain.

The 'supervisor survives desktop' check proves the Gateway still serves HTTP after the desktop exits; it does not run a full research-agent/Supervisor workflow. The desktop has no Supervisor lifecycle control, so the architectural claim is sound, but the evidence is Gateway availability.

DPAPI protection is asserted through safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()=true, the Windows platform value and the ciphertext-only envelope; I did not decrypt the envelope with an external DPAPI tool or test a different Windows user profile.

The packaged renderer is driven via a loopback --remote-debugging-port test switch; process/window introspection and a PrintWindow desktop screenshot cross-check it, but there is no native mouse/keyboard injection.

V0 has no external-link surface: window.open and foreign navigation are denied and shell.openExternal is not registered, so the task card's validated external-browser-open step has no entry point (P3 finding).
The internal Windows artifact is unsigned by design (PE security directory size 0); external distribution would require an operator-provided signing certificate.
The Node gate command is correctly marked external because a cold cache needs the npm registry; both gate runs used an already-warm store, so the cold-download path was not exercised in this review.

The implementer's authoritative Windows evidence (135449) predates the gate run that reset the shared _test database, so that exact database state is not retained; my fresh-seed rerun against ravel_t14_review_test reproduced the full flow.

My independent gate logs live at /tmp/t14-review-evidence/T14/run-20261020-141155 (WSL) and are not committed, because this review may only add docs/premium/reviews/T14/1.json. The committed implementer manifest and Windows evidence remain the repository record.
acceptance-map.json keeps T14 at RUNNING and this review does not modify it; integration into main and any status transition remain the Supervisor's decision.
